draft.title: Proofs with angle properties
card: Known angle facts can be used as reasons. Angles in a triangle add to 180°. Angles on a straight line add to 180°. Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal.
A proof chains these facts. Each step is a statement with a reason, and each step builds on earlier ones.
The exterior angle of a triangle is the angle formed outside by extending one side. Example: the interior angle at C is c, and the other two angles are a and b.
Then a + b + c = 180° (angles in a triangle). The exterior angle at C is 180° − c (angles on a straight line). So the exterior angle = a + b.
draft.remember: Chain known angle facts, giving a reason at every step, to prove a new result.

a.q: In the proof, which reason shows that the exterior angle at C equals 180° − c?
opts: Angles on a straight line add to 180°
Angles in a triangle add to 180°
Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal
Vertically opposite angles are equal
a.why: The exterior angle and angle c sit side by side on a straight line, so together they make 180°. The triangle fact gives a + b + c = 180°, which is a different step.
a.clue: The exterior angle and c lie together along one line.

b.q: In triangle PQR, angle P = 50° and angle Q = 70°. Side QR is extended to S. Which pair of steps proves that the exterior angle PRS is 120°?
opts: R = 60° (angles in a triangle), then PRS = 180° − 60° (straight line)
R = 60° (angles in a triangle), then PRS = 60° + 60° (straight line)
R = 120° (angles in a triangle), then PRS = 120° (exterior)
R = 60° (alternate angles), then PRS = 180° − 60° (straight line)
b.why: The triangle gives angle R = 180° − 50° − 70° = 60°. Then PRS and R are on a straight line, so PRS = 180° − 60° = 120°. There are no parallel lines here, so alternate angles cannot be used as a reason.
b.clue: Find angle R first, then use the straight line.
